Only the drug name is quarantined (two review_only facts, one per side); the dose increase to 20 mg for an additional week stays a scored fact with a generic name.

The text reports minimal improvement in pure-tone thresholds after the dose increase (right 48.8 dB, left 47.5 dB), whereas the Figure 3A caption says pure-tone thresholds were the same. The qualitative wording differs; no numbers conflict.

The comprehensive MRI of the orbit, cervical neck and whole spine prompted by the earlier MR, and the MRI that revealed demyelinating lesions at T4–T5 one week after admission, are not identified by the source as the same study; they are kept separate.

Right-sided hearing recovery is dated "approximately one month after the onset" in the text, while the Figure 1 caption says "After 6 weeks". These approximate intervals differ and no exact dates are used here.

The text says there were no significant changes "immediately after the treatment" (intratympanic injections), whereas the Figure 2 caption says pure-tone thresholds were not recovered "after 3 weeks" of injection. The interval after treatment is not identified as the same.

The first plan of three intratympanic dexamethasone sessions (right-sided episode) is not stated as delivered. The later phrases "rather than by ITDI" and "the same regimen as the previous treatment" imply it may have been given, but the source never states it, so it stays planned; the text also suggests recovery may have come from systemic steroids rather than the injections.
Three months "after the onset" is not explicitly tied to the bilateral episode in the sentence; the Figure 3 caption says 3 months after the bilateral loss.

The same-assessment speech reception and discrimination results are in sentences following the one that carries the stated time; their time is not borrowed, so only the sentences stating a time carry one.

Discussion sentences about the literature (Cogan syndrome comparison, speech discrimination recovery pattern, systemic steroids as standard) are author interpretation or cited-series conclusions, not separate patient facts; the Cogan syndrome comparison is not a documented diagnosis or exclusion for this patient.
